rationale: req_q depends on synchronized a2_q, but ack_q is driven only by dst_ready_i and never by r2_q, so only one direction depends on the opposite synchronizer: CDC-015 WARNING Heuristic. Reader A's note is right that CDC-013 stays active (no unique reciprocal pair, both source periods below 1.5x); those are additional findings on a bad case and do not change the label.

author_reading.rationale: Request crosses to dst, but the acknowledge register follows only local dst_ready_i and ignores the synchronized request: one-way dependency on the reciprocal synchronizer.

labels.rationale: The request can clear based on the returned acknowledge, but ack_q depends only on dst_ready_i. An already-high ready bit can clear a request without receiver observation. Only the request leg depends on the opposite synchronizer.
labels.suspected_flaw: The malformed pair leaves CDC-013 active. Both source periods are below the respective 1.5-period review margins.

labels.rationale: req_q (clk_a) is cleared by the synchronized acknowledge a2_q (design.sv:20), and req_q is synchronized into clk_b via r1_q -> r2_q (design.sv:29-30), but the return acknowledge register ack_q (design.sv:33) is driven solely by dst_ready_i with no dependency on r2_q, forming a one-way structural handshake mismatch (CDC-015 WARNING Heuristic).
